name: Register a custom field and show it with a Paragraph binding
query: My plugin registers a 'book' post type. Add an ISBN field that editors can edit in the block editor and show it on the single book template inside a normal Paragraph block, without writing a custom block.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router and wp-project-triage to locate the plugin
Step 2: Search the plugin for existing meta registrations and bindings
Step 3: Confirm the post type has show_in_rest true and supports custom-fields (add it if missing)
Step 4: Register the key with register_post_meta() on init for the book post type: type string, single true, default, label, sanitize_callback, auth_callback, show_in_rest true
Step 5: Use a key without a leading underscore so core/post-meta can output it
Step 6: Add a Paragraph with metadata.bindings.content set to source core/post-meta and args.key set to the ISBN key, with fallback text
Step 7: Verify the key appears in the post type's REST schema and that the front end prints the meta value instead of the fallback
success_criteria: Uses register_post_meta() (or register_meta() with object_subtype) scoped to the post type
Sets single true and show_in_rest true
Provides sanitize_callback and an auth_callback that checks edit_post for the post
Does not use a protected (underscore-prefixed) key for the bound field
Ensures custom-fields support on the custom post type
Binding markup uses source core/post-meta with args.key and targets the content attribute
Does not create a custom block for this task
Explains that posts without a value render an empty paragraph, not the fallback text
